While wins and losses are the primary metric used by evaluators to determine whether a week was successful or not in the NFL, individual matchups most certainly matters. The final game of the Week 9 slate presented an enchanting one for NFL hardcores — Seahawks star Jaxon Smith-Njigba against anyone who the Bears lined up against him. Smith-Njigba is football's best receiver. His place at the top of that ladder hasn't been under question since the start of last year. And yet, there's a case — albeit a quiet one — that Chicago made him looking decidedly more ordinary than usual in its 34-17 win. Here's how the Bears bottled up Smith-Njigba to propel Ben Johnson's side to a famous win over Seattle. item.title: Kane Exits With Injury in Blackhawks 5-2 Loss To Avalanche
item.description: The Chicago Blackhawks (4-10-1) blew a multi-goal lead for the second straight game, giving up five unanswered goals in a 5-2 loss to the Colorado Avalanche (9-5-1) at the United Center. The Blackhawks have now lost six of their last seven games Wyatt Kaiser and Roman Kantserov scored to give the Blackhawks a 2-0 lead just 7:05 into the game, but the Avalanche defense and goaltender Mackenzie Blackwood shut them down over the final 52:55. That’s now six of the last seven games in which they’ve failed to score three goals. Nazem Kadri and Jaden Schwartz each scored twice for Colorado, who’ve now won 14 of 18 meetings with the Blackhawks since the start of 2022. Blackwood stopped 21 of 23 shots to earn the win in net, while Devon Toews scored the empty netter. To make matters worse, the Blackhawks lost star forward Patrick Kane due to injury in the second period, with head coach Jeff Blashill announcing the future Hall of Famer will miss the next couple of games with an upper-body issue. The Blackhawks have a three-game road trip ahead on the schedule, where they’ll face the Florida Panthers, Tampa Bay Lightning, and Carolina Hurricanes. Even with Kane in the lineup, winning any of those games would be challenging. Now, the Blackhawks are put in an even greater bind without one of their premier forwards. Here are highlights from the Blackhawks 5-2 loss to the Avalanche, dropping their 2026-27 regular-season record to 4-10-1 in 15 games. First Period Kaiser’s wrist shot from the point was deflected, but the puck still trickled across the goal line just 57 seconds in, giving the Blackhawks an early 1-0 lead. Kaiser has now recorded a point in three of his last four games and has two goals this season. Chicago has scored first in five of the last six outings. item.description: After a rough homecoming performance at McCamish Pavilion, in which the Jackets were swept by both #2 Pitt and #7 SMU, the Jackets hit the road over Halloween weekend to face the Notre Dame Fighting Irish and the #3 Louisville Cardinals. The Jackets split the weekend, completing a dramatic reverse sweep of Notre Dame before falling to the Cardinals in straight sets. This puts the Jackets at 14-8 on the year and 6-5 in the ACC, keeping pace in the conference and showing notable improvement over last season. VS Notre Dame Unlike their football (and lacrosse and fencing teams, which are apparently even more dominant than football), the Notre Dame volleyball team is, well, terrible. The Irish entered the matchup against the Jackets at a miserable 4-15, including 1-9 in ACC play. That was good for second-to-last in the ACC, ahead of a somehow even worse Syracuse team, which had provided the Irish with their sole Power Four win of the year. The point is, this should have been a walk in the park for the Jackets, and yet, two sets in, Tech was on the verge of being swept. The Irish ran an incredibly clean operation, hitting .433 on the set and tallying just three total errors to the Jackets’ 11. Alida Bennour was largely responsible for keeping Tech alive, contributing nine kills and an ace. item.title: Rob Wright, BYU Offense Shine in Opening Night Win Over Ohio State
item.description: SALT LAKE CITY, UT - NOVEMBER 2: Robert Wright III #1 of the Brigham Young Cougars drives the ball the court against Justin Pippen #10 of the Ohio State Buckeyes during the first half of their game at the Delta Center on November 2, 2026 in Salt Lake City, Utah. (Photo by Chris Gardner/Getty Images) | Getty Images After scoring just 16 points in the first 13 minutes, BYU’s offense woke up in a big way the rest of the game in a 94-83 win over Ohio State on the opening day of college basketball. BYU was down 37-34 at halftime and trailed by as much as 11, but BYU outscored the Buckeyes 60-46 in the second half. Rob Wright was sensational and looked like an All-American, leading BYU with 33 points, 5 assists, and 1 turnover on 9/15 shooting from the field (4/5 from three) and 11/12 from the line. Rob showed his whole bag, getting into the paint, finishing around the rim and with floaters, and hitting pullup and stepback threes. All five BYU starters scored in double figures. Tyler Betsey was 4/5 from three and scored 15 points, Collin Chandler scored 15 points as well, Bruce Branch put up 12 after a slow start, and Jaxon Kohler scored 11 points. BYU played four guys off the bench, who scored a combined 8 points. Nate Pickens made a three to end the first half and Brooks Bahr played nice defense on Ohio State’s best player, John Mobley. BYU shot 54% compared to 49% from Ohio State, shot 11/24 (46%) from three, and won the turnover battle 12-8. BYU’s defense didn’t play great, but they did enough and came up with a few good stretches to allow them to extend the league. BYU’s lack of rim protection will put a ceiling on the defense, and Ohio State exposed that at times around the rim. This game should hold up as a Quad 1 win for BYU and be a nice data point on the resume. Ohio State came into the game ranked 18 in KenPom and BYU 33. BYU jumped to 22 after the win. BYU next plays Omaha Friday night in Provo and has the runway to be 5-0 going into the Maui Invitational in 3 weeks.

item.title: Jaxon Smith-Njigba receiving yards pace: How Seahawks WR can catch Calvin Johnson, Cooper Kupp
item.description: Jaxon Smith-Njigba receiving yards pace: How Seahawks WR can catch Calvin Johnson, Cooper Kupp originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Somehow, Jaxon Smith-Njigba may be even more dominant this season than he was in 2025. The Seahawks receiver has stamped himself as the NFL's best offensive weapon, coming off an outstanding 2025 season in which he was named Offensive Player of the Year while helping lead Seattle to a Super Bowl title. But through the first seven games of 2026, Smith-Njigba could be on pace for history. Last year, he finished No. 8 on the all-time leaderboard for single-season receiving yards with 1,793. This year, he's not only on pace to shatter that mark for a new career-high — he could contend for Calvin Johnson's record. Here's a look at where Smith-Njigba's pace stands against Johnson's historic 2012 season. Through eight games, he is on pace to shatter his career-highs in catches, yards and touchdowns, all set last season. He's already just one touchdown shy of his entire 2025 total over 17 games. And he's been the full engine of Seattle's offense — the run game ranks around the middle of the NFL with 109.6 yards per game, yet Smith-Njigba is accountable for more yards than all other Seahawks receivers combined. Jaxon Smith-Njigba has 959 yards receiving and 9 TD catches this season. And at his current pace of 123.2 yards per game, he'd make NFL history without even needing a 17th game. Here's more to know about Smith-Njigba's pace. How many yards does Jaxon Smith-Njigba need to pass Calvin Johnson? It's still fairly early in the record chance, but entering Week 8, Smith-Njigba is 979 yards away from tying, and 980 yards away from breaking, Johnson's 2012 record of 1,964 receiving yards. In 2012, Johnson averaged 122.8 yards per game over 16 games. That means Smith-Njigba is currently out-pacing him — and if he maintains that pace, he wouldn't even need a 17th game to break the record. item.title: Marist football miss late FG try, fall at San Diego
item.description: Marist missed a field goal try with 43 seconds left in regulation and bowed to San Diego, 41-40, at Torero Stadium on Saturday, October 31. Consecutive losses have dropped Marist to 4-5 and 3-2 in the Pioneer Football League. San Diego bumped to 4-5, 3-3. The Red Foxes trailed 35-26 headed into the fourth quarter and produced a pair of touchdowns, the last on a 51-yard run by Isaiah Simmons (his second of the game, the first on a stutter-step move from 35 yards) with 6:17 left for a 40-35 lead - he finished with 182 yards on 21 carries. Simmons took a handoff to the right side and cut inside a block and ran untouched. The Toreros used a no-huddle offense to move 65 yards on nine plays. USD quarterback Dom Nankil completed four of five throws and ran the final 4 yards for the go-ahead touchdown, faking a handoff, deking one tackler and diving in with 2:48 to play (a 2-point conversion failed). Logan Johnson returned the ensuing kickoff 28 yards to the Marist 33. Quarterback Sonny Mannino gained a trio of first downs, the first on his own 4-yard run on fourth down and following with completions of 10 and 28 yards to Zach Garmont, down to the San Diego 19. Simmons gained 8 yards up the middle but then suffered a 3-yard loss. Lincoln Cardillo was stopped shy of the first down, and Luke Stenson was called on for a 30-yard field goal try but missed. Mannino passed for 265 yards and ran for 34. Sophomore defensive back Jace Williamson set the school's Div. I single-game mark with 22 tackles. Marist took a 19-7 lead midway through the second quarter but the Toreros scored the next 21 points, and eventually took a 35-26 lead into the fourth. But the Red Foxes responded with a pair of touchdowns, San Diego improved to 17-2 all-time against Marist, including all 12 games at home. Marist closes with home games against Morehead State on Nov. 7 and Butler on Nov. 14 and a road contest at Davidson on Nov. 21. kmcmillan@th-record.com X / Twitter: @KenMcMillanTHR This article originally appeared on Times Herald-Record: Marist football miss late FG try, fall at San Diego

item.title: Why NASCAR's indecision led to Dodge's decision to return to Cup
item.description: Motorsport photo Dodge is coming back to the NASCAR Cup Series in 2027 with Kaulig Racing but there are caveats aplenty. The body has been approved, with an unveil scheduled for the Snowball Derby Super Late race in December, but the engine inside of the car is not expected to be a proprietary Stellantis or MOPAR built platform. Current reporting suggests AJ Allmendinger and Ty Dillon will drive cars powered by Earnhardt Childress Racing Engines next season. In some ways, NASCAR was fortunate in that Stellantis was only interested in racing right now using an internal combustion gasoline platform that aligned with the 'HEMI is Back' initiative from the manufacturer. It wasn't that long ago that NASCAR was seriously all-in towards electric and hybrid before the culture domestically shifted. Stellantis, Dodge and RAM reflects that shift and NASCAR hadn't yet jumped into the EV space. NASCAR Event Management president John Probst said that wasn’t a selling point to Stellantis but all parties benefited from the timing. "I'd like to pretend we had some big scheme that made that all look good, but it's just like a lot of things in life," Probst said. "Sometimes it's just timing works out and you're aligned, and this is the example of that." Probst also said that at a minimum, NASCAR will retain its current engine regulations through 2028 but also could extend it through 2030 or 2032. In other words, there were few reasons for Dodge to build their own engine just to have to do it again in two to five years. So again, the timing just made sense for Dodge. Probst conceded that they nearly prematurely ended up with an EV platform at the moment the country turned on them. Thus, NASCAR is being thoughtful about what comes next. "I would say that right now we have started discussions with the OEMs about what does our future look like around the engine," Probst said. "I would say that we're targeting anywhere from 2030-to-2032, and that may sound a little wishy-washy, I guess, on the specific date, but as we talk through the OEMs, we've already had our first meeting. We're onto our second meeting here coming up real soon to try and figure out where we want to go as a sport. "And I think that some of that is looking at the broader landscape around what's going on in the motor sport world and us, what do we want to do, frankly, around our engine? If you look around the landscape, there's certainly been a lot of vacillation around how much of the powertrain should be electrified. So, we just want to make sure that we don't rush into something. "If we would've rushed in a few years ago, we'd add a big hybrid component to the car. And I think that there's just a lot that goes into it. So I guess it's a lot of words for probably what could have been a quick answer. 2030 to 2032 is the window we're looking at." item.title: Swift, Simmons star as Bears maul Seahawks
item.description: D'Andre Swift rushes for one of his three touchdowns in Chicago's road victory over Seattle (Steph Chambers) D'Andre Swift rushed for three touchdowns as the Chicago Bears overpowered the Seattle Seahawks 34-17 in a statement road victory over the reigning Super Bowl champions on Monday. Chicago running back Swift scored all three of his touchdowns in the second half at Seattle's Lumen Field, two of them coming in the fourth quarter as the Seahawks threatened a comeback. A rampant Chicago defense led by newly signed defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons also helped shut down Seattle's offense. Simmons, traded to the Bears last week from the Tennessee Titans, enjoyed a dream debut with six tackles and a sack. "I'm so excited to be a Chicago Bear man," Simmons told ESPN. "This is just the beginning. We've got some stuff to clean up but it's a good football team and I’m happy to be a part of it." Chicago quarterback Caleb Williams finished with 247 passing yards with 24-of-34 completions and one touchdown. Swift had 69 yards from 27 carries for his three touchdowns. Seattle fell to 4-4 to lose further ground in the NFC West behind San Francisco (6-1). The Bears set the tone for an impressive win in the first quarter when Williams led a 17-play 80-yard drive that ended with a touchdown pass to Luther Burden. Seattle kicker Jason Myers got Seattle's first points with a 27-yard field goal but Chicago responded with back-to-back three-pointers from Cairo Santos to leave the Bears 13-3 up. Seattle quarterback Sam Darnold found Jaxon Smith-Njigba with a 43-yard pass to leave Seattle only four points adrift at the break. But Swift capped another long Chicago drive to score his first touchdown in the third quarter and give the Bears a comfortable 20-9 lead. Seattle responded with a Cooper Kupp touchdown early in the fourth quarter but Chicago's defense took over and Swift bagged two touchdowns to seal victory. rcw/pst

item.title: NFL world reacts to Bears' dominant 34-17 win vs. Seahawks
item.description: The Chicago Bears made another statement on the prime-time stage with a dominant 34-17 win over the defending Super Bowl champion Seattle Seahawks to improve to 6-2 on the season, where the team's biggest playmakers, quarterback Caleb Williams and new defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons, shined. Simmons' debut with Chicago couldn't have gone better, as he tied for a team-high six tackles, including two tackles for loss, one sack, one QB hit and one pass breakup in what was a sensational defensive showing. He opened up things for players around him, most notably former college teammate Montez Sweat, who had one sack and three QB hits. Simmons is already proving to be worth those two first-round picks (and perhaps more). Meanwhile, Williams cemented himself in the MVP conversation after putting on a show against a dominant Seahawks defense. He completed 24-of-34 passes for 247 yards with one touchdown, no turnovers and a 101 passer rating. Williams became the first quarterback to throw for more than 200 yards against this Seattle defense this season. In the last two weeks, Chicago has beaten the defending AFC Champions (New England Patriots) and reigning Super Bowl champions (Seahawks). item.title: Florida State dominates FAMU in season opener, 112-69
item.description: We are so back. Florida State (0-0, 0-0 ACC) played Florida A&M (0-0, 0-0 SWAC) in Tampa as part of the Orion180 Tipoff Classic on Monday night. The Seminoles, looking to build on a top-20 recruiting class and start the season off right, did just that, winning 112-69 to move to 1-0. First Half It was a disappointing first half if you consider three-pointers. The Seminoles made just three of 12 triples. However, they excelled in virtually every other category. FSU kept their foot on the gas and never looked back, as there were zero lead changes whatsoever. Not much to say in terms of this game being competitive; the closest the game got was 13-8. It was all FSU from there on out. Marcis Ponder got seven boards in the first half alone, while also tacking on five two-pointers and five made free throws. He also got the lone block for Florida State. Second Half After the poor shooting performance in the first, the second was admittedly better, as they finished at 8/24 for 33% of their made threes. The defense looked like last year’s team but only way better and with more size behind it. The bench also showed some promise; Brandon Bass Jr. and Martay Barnes led with 13 and 10 points, respectively. Alex Steen was six and seven in points and rebounds (get it?), while Cooper Schwieger scored six points and got two rebounds. The Seminoles finished with an offensive rating of 142.4 and a defensive efficiency rating of 87.7. Yes, it’s a SWAC non-conference game. Finishing with seven total turnovers is absurd, even against a weaker team. If they keep up this pace, even somewhat against Troy or even Florida, this could be a very scary team. Players of the Game Sebastian Rancik was in a league of his own with 25 points in just 27 minutes, a new career high for him. I’d also like to shout out Marcis Ponder for dropping 15 points and 11 rebounds. What’s Next? Florida State returns home to Tallahassee for their home opener against the Troy Trojans, a tournament team in 2025, on November 6th. Fans can catch that game on the ACC Network Extra. Then it’s a huge home game against the No. 1 team in the land, *thunder sound effect* , the Florida Gators, followed by a gimme game versus Texas A&M Corpus Christi.

Now, it looks as though the Diamondbacks are looking to put up a more conscious effort to trade Marte away after a drama-filled 2026 campaign. However, MLB insider Jim Bowden warned Arizona that it might not be very easy to trade the 33-year-old away, especially when he has a no-trade clause. “If he decides that he doesn’t want to get traded, then he won’t be,” Bowden said. “You gotta find a team that not only that he’s willing to go to, but you gotta find a front office, a GM, a manager, and a group of players that are willing to accept all the things that come with Ketel Marte, which includes times where players, some teammates, have been disappointed that he didn’t take the field.” Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Trading Ketel Marte is A LOT easier said than done. @JimBowdenGM breaks down the no-trade clause, the contract, and everything a team would have to weigh before making a deal. pic.twitter.com/IJWNBJxihC — Foul Territory (@FoulTerritoryTV) November 2, 2026 Marte missed the Diamondbacks’ August 17 clash against the Boston Red Sox despite being penciled into the starting lineup, and this absence of his stunned the organization. item.description: Photo by Emilee Chinn/Getty Images LeBron James taking a sip of a fan’s drink has become the biggest talking point from the game between the Philadelphia 76ers and the Chicago Bulls. A longtime Sixers season-ticket holder, Clemons was walking back to his seat with a drink in his hand, and James crashed into him. The wine spilt everywhere, but to his surprise, the 76ers superstar grabbed it and took a sip of it before heading back on the court to continue playing. I’m not worried about the wine getting on me.” A glass that James took a sip from in the middle of an NBA game would’ve been good memorabilia for many fans to hold on to or even sell. item.title: Dortmund bring back painful memories for evergreen Pellegrini
item.description: Real Betis coach Manuel Pellegrini heads back to the scene of one of the most painful nights of his career (JORGE GUERRERO) Veteran Real Betis coach Manuel Pellegrini has regularly produced impressive results at the highest level but his failure to win the Champions League means some hesitate to place him among the managerial elite. The 73-year-old's team boast three wins from three in the league phase ahead of Wednesday's visit to face Borussia Dortmund, the scene of one of the most agonising defeats in his long career. In 2013 Pellegrini's Malaga conceded twice in injury time against Jurgen Klopp's Dortmund, to miss out on a Champions League semi-final berth. It was an especially cruel defeat for Pellegrini, who had attended his father's funeral in Chile before landing in Germany on the morning of the match. "They did not want us in the semi-finals," complained Pellegrini about the officiating afterwards, with Felipe Santana's winner seemingly scored from an offside position. That summer Pellegrini moved to Manchester City, winning the Premier League and two League Cups before departing in 2016, without a Champions League trophy. The evergreen Chilean joined Betis in 2020 and is now enjoying the longest spell in charge of a club in his career. Pellegrini has stayed faithful to the idea that his teams must entertain and Betis fit the bill, boasting a host of exciting attackers like Isco and Ez Abde. Pellegrini, who graduated in civil engineering in 1979 while playing at Universidad de Chile, took Betis to their first final in 17 years, winning the Copa del Rey in 2022. Last season he steered the Andalusians back to Champions League qualification after two decades away from the elite. "We started the first match of the season... and at the end of the team talk we wrote in green letters -- 'today we begin our journey to the Champions League'," explained Pellegrini in May. - 'My own' way - Pellegrini returning Betis to the big-time is no surprise, given his track record. The coach turned Villarreal into a Champions League semi-finalist in 2006, with his team knocked out by Arsenal. Juan Roman Riquelme missed a last-gasp penalty in the second leg which could have taken the game to extra-time on Spain's east coast. Pellegrini led Villarreal to a second-place finish in La Liga in 2008, finishing above giants Barcelona and Atletico Madrid. His success earned him the Real Madrid job in 2009, where he achieved a then-club record 96 points, but was sacked at the end of the season to make way for Jose Mourinho. item.title: Demichelis brings 'competitive aura' to Leipzig before City reunion
item.description: RB Leipzig coach Martin Demichelis will face his former side Manchester City on Wednesday (Javier SORIANO) Coach Martin Demichelis will be looking to strike a blow against his former employers when his RB Leipzig side host Manchester City in the Champions League on Wednesday. Former Argentina centre-back Demichelis spent three seasons at Manchester City, winning the 2013-14 Premier League title and two League Cups. Demichelis, who also won four league titles as a player at Bayern Munich, is now hoping to bring success to Saxony in a budding coaching career. Leipzig have beaten City just once in six attempts, but may feel Enzo Maresca's men are vulnerable. In their past three games, City have lost twice and won the other match on penalties, as the spectre of sanctions for breaching financial rules looms. Demichelis, 45, was controversially handpicked by then-Red Bull boss Jurgen Klopp to take over in the summer. To bring in Demichelis, Leipzig sacked popular coach Ole Werner, who had taken a young team back into the Champions League, while overseeing the development of Yan Diomande. Real Madrid paid a reported 125 million euros ($140 million) for Diomande, just a year after Leipzig signed him for 20 million euros. Demichelis was relegated from La Liga during a short stint with Mallorca last season but Klopp and Leipzig had seen enough to convince them of his ability, after he oversaw a significant up-turn in the club's form. After a rocky start with Leipzig including a 4-1 loss at Como in the Champions League and a 6-1 thrashing by Bayern Munich, Leipzig have won three games in a row. The Red Bulls sit just three points off top spot in the Bundesliga, but are in desperate need of points in Europe. The 2020 semi-finalists are 29th in the 36-team table after winning just one of three Champions League games this campaign. - 'Competitive aura' - Demichelis benefited from the tutelage of several big-name coaches, including Louis van Gaal, Manuel Pellegrini, Diego Simeone and his idol Diego Maradona. Leipzig centre-back Maxime Esteve said Demichelis has brought a "competitive aura" to the club.
